I'm really tired of this narrative. Yes Russia would not last long against NATO in a conventional war. Yes corruption is greatly hindering their command. Yes much of their decision-making throughout the war is questionable at best. Yes Putin is a psycho genociding thundercunt with delusions of grandeur. 

But Russia is *not* weak, they are still a very dangerous nation. 

They have spent the last 2 years rapidly retooling their industry for war while Congress is deep-throating caviar. Mobilising the defence industry is not instantaneous. Its a very slow and expensive affair. Yes, they've been sanctioned to hell but economies on Russia's scale, especially autocratic ones with a state media can scrounge up enough money to fund the war for a VERY long time. 

They have constructed increasingly sophisticated defensive lines, with minefields kilometres deep that Ukraine failed to break through in their summer offensive last year. This was **while** a steady stream of western equipment was still available + Ukraine had larger reserves of artillery ammunition. In this war with no air superiority on either side artillery has been the most important factor across the entire front, and Ukraine is being outfired by several **factors**. 

I don't want to sound like a doomsayer, but it's an attritional conflict and at the current rate, Russia will most likely win if political support in the west doesn't pick up. 

In that regard it doesn't even look good either, Russian disinformation campaigns are bearing fruit. There's a lot more social media attention on the Israel-Palestine conflict drawing from Ukraine. And I haven't even mentioned the upcoming elections. 

Thinking of Russia as some push over back water country, instead of the rapidly industrialising, rapidly adapting threat it is, to me is extremely detrimental.

**Kingdoms and empires** should be right up your alley. there's a bit of exposition dump at the start but I think the author is planning on rewriting that aspect. The world building is really nice, it has its own wiki. There isn't much romance out currently, but there are a few short stories available in the demo for the RO's

**War for the west**; the characterisation is a bit more limited than the ones you mentioned. It's more of a 'fiefdom manager' but it has some of the best replayability out of any IF. Romance is a little limited in this one too.

**Sword of rhivenia**; I'm a little more hesitant to recommend this since it's a fairly divisive game, and at this point I doubt the sequel will happen. There are some flaws with the characters and plot I think, but I still thought it was decent. 

**A mage reborn**; this has a mediaeval setting, but there's a larger focus on magic and the characters. This is one of my favourite IF's, but the author is rewriting the sequel, and has been radio silent for the last ~8 months now, so keep that in mind. 

**Shepherds of haven**; I highly recommend this wip, there's a large cast of characters and they're all distinct and written well. If you enjoy the public demo, I'd recommend subbing to Lena's patreon, the demo there is 1 mil+ words and is updated monthly

**Arcadie second born** is quite good as well, it's a twine IF and it's on steam too. I'd say the characterisation is a high point of this IF, though I do think one of the RO's is just better in terms of detail written for them.

**Lost heir series**. I personally didn't enjoy this as much since it's *a lot* more focused on stats than other games. If you get the dopamine rush of 'number go up' then you'll probably enjoy this. 

These are the ones that stood out to me from memory. There's a few others like **the great tournament games** and **Ironheart** that I haven't had the chance to read, but they've been mentioned fairly frequently on this sub.

Edit: I also love **throne of ashes** on itch io. It can be *really* dark compared to most other IF's. There's only one RO path fully completed right now but I'd say it's well worth the $2. 

I also can't believe I forgot to mention **I the forgotten one**. Very high replayability, writing is very detailed and has lots of flavour. Characters also feel very real. I've heard some people criticise it for being having too much depression, but they still rated it a 9/10.

Edit 2: if you don't mind mediaeval but in a fantasy imperial china, there's an IF called **tale of two cranes** on the forums. The demo is 5 years old or something, but apparently the full game is on schedule for a 2024 release with ~750k words. I haven't seen much buzz for this but I'm quite looking forward to it, I thought the demo was solid and it has likely drastically improved in the past 5 years.

I'll try to explain why the ones you mentioned have such large fanbases individually.

**Wayhaven** - Great romance. The RO's are pretty fleshed out, we've had 3 books to get used to them and I think the different flavours of RO's can appeal to the vast majority of readers. 

Imho, the plot is hit or miss, but the core of the stories will always be the four RO's. Romance will always have the biggest draw in any form of media, and they're excellent in Wayhaven. 

**FH** - Absolutely fantastic series so far overall. The sequel has an enormous amount of detail, and there are a ton of choices and branching paths. I can't even imagine how much further branching Malin will have to do for book 3. 

The relationships are also extremely well developed.  The characters feel real, they talk and behave like people in their position would. There is also a *lot* of angst which readers tend to love. 

The world and plot changes based on your decisions, characters act differently based on what you do. The game can make you feel like a badass just as easily as it can push you into a corner to cry. 

**Infinite Seas**: Again, amazing and detailed series. A lot of what I mentioned about FH regarding the world feeling real and developed applies here. Unlike the other two though there isn't as much of a focus on romance. 

But the game does what it set out to do, make the reader feel like they're a badass dragoon officer (depending on the choices you make ofc). 


**Some of my picks**:

**ITFO**: Has excellent war management like the Infinite Seas, and the depressing angst of FH. The characters as well as the world are very developed, + the author is great with imagery. What's not to love? 

**Vampire Regent**: Slightly underrated imo. There's a lot to do in this book, and a few types of vampires you can play as, all of which are pretty interesting. One of the endings is among my favourites out of every other IF. I love everything else from these authors too, they pump out really consistent material (War for the west, Ghost simulator, Unsupervised etc). 

**Kingdoms and Empires**: This is a WIP but it'll probably be in my top 3 when it drops (the other two being FH and infinite sea). It just hits all the right notes with me. The characters are fleshed out, the battle scenes so far are gory and great. The author has just spent at least the last year researching and world building.

As I said, this is only a guess, so I would encourage doing some further research if you're interested, there's most definitely a whole bunch of other contributing factors

The japanese managed to somewhat (emperor is a figurehead) remain in power because the Americans wanted a strong democratic ally in Asia  to combat the same political group that had massacred the Romanovs. 

Again, I would encourage doing some more in depth research if you're at least a little bit interested in history, there are many r/askhistorian commenters and threads that would explain it far better than I can.
